title: JavaScript Project-Based Learning Core Check
description: Check your understanding of planning, organizing, building, testing, refactoring, documenting, and deploying JavaScript projects.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of project-based learning?

options.text: To combine individual concepts into complete, useful projects
To avoid planning and write code randomly
To replace JavaScript fundamentals with only HTML
To memorize one exact app forever

questions.explanation: Project-based learning helps you connect separate skills into complete workflows with real behavior and trade-offs.

questions.prompt: Which is the best example of a testable requirement?

options.text: The user can add a non-empty task and see it in the task list
The app should feel nice
The code should be amazing
The project should have many features

questions.explanation: A testable requirement describes specific behavior that can be checked.

options.text: Specific conditions that define when a feature is done
A list of every feature you might ever add
CSS rules for accepting form input
A replacement for testing

questions.explanation: Acceptance criteria describe the observable behavior required for a feature to be considered complete.

questions.prompt: Why should a first project version stay small?

options.text: A small version is easier to finish, test, and improve
Small projects cannot have bugs
JavaScript cannot support more than one feature
Deployment only works for unfinished projects

questions.explanation: A focused version one gives you a realistic finish line and a stable base for extensions.

questions.prompt: What is a milestone in a project?

options.text: A small, complete step that produces visible progress
A comment placed every 100 lines
A random file name
A feature that is never tested

questions.explanation: Milestones split a project into manageable, testable deliverables.

questions.prompt: In a browser project, what should usually be the source of truth?

options.text: Application state stored in objects and arrays
Only the text currently visible in DOM elements
A random console log
The CSS file

questions.explanation: The DOM should display state. The main data should usually live in clear JavaScript objects and arrays.

questions.prompt: Which flow is common for browser app interactions?

options.text: User action -> event handler -> state update -> render UI
CSS -> API -> delete state -> ignore user action
Render once -> never update anything
Console log -> automatic deployment -> form validation

questions.explanation: Most interactive browser apps respond to events by updating state and rendering the current state.

questions.prompt: Why are stable IDs useful in list-based apps?

options.text: They let you update, delete, or identify the correct item even if the array order changes
They make CSS unnecessary
They automatically save data to an API
They prevent all runtime errors

questions.explanation: Stable IDs identify items reliably. Array indexes can change after sorting, inserting, or deleting.

questions.prompt: What should an API-based project usually show while waiting for data?

options.text: A loading state
Only a syntax error
A secret API key
Nothing until the whole project is rewritten

questions.explanation: Loading, success, empty, and error states make API projects understandable to users.

options.text: After the current behavior works and can be checked
Before any behavior exists
Only while the app is broken
Instead of testing

questions.explanation: Refactoring should preserve behavior, so it is safer when the existing behavior is already working and testable.

questions.prompt: Which DOM API is usually safer for inserting user-provided text?

options.text: `textContent`
`innerHTML`
`eval()`
`document.write()`

questions.explanation: `textContent` inserts text instead of parsing the value as HTML.

questions.prompt: What should a useful project README include?

options.text: A short description, features, setup steps, and notes about how the project works
Only the word README
Private API keys
Unrelated code copied from another project

questions.explanation: A README should help someone understand, run, and evaluate the project.
